subject: math

objective.text: Use rectangular arrays to investigate odd and even numbers.

explanations.title: Even plus even
explanations.text: Join two even arrays. The total is even. 6 plus 8 equals 14. 14 is even.

explanations.title: Even plus odd
explanations.text: An odd number has one tile sticking out. Join an even and an odd and one tile still sticks out. The total is odd.

explanations.title: Odd plus odd
explanations.text: Two odd numbers each have one tile sticking out. The two extra tiles make a pair. The total is even.

explanations.title: It works for bigger numbers
explanations.text: The same rules work for larger numbers. 10 plus 12 equals 22. Both addends are even and the total is even.

explanations.title: Skip-count by twos
explanations.text: Count by ones and knock on the twos. Then say only the twos: 2, 4, 6, 8 and on to 20.

examples.title: 6 plus 8
examples.text: 2 rows of 3 and 2 rows of 4 join to make 2 rows of 7. That is 14. 14 is even.

examples.title: 6 plus 7
examples.text: 2 rows of 3 and 2 rows of 3 with 1 extra tile. That is 13. One tile sticks out. 13 is odd.

examples.title: 7 plus 9
examples.text: 7 and 9 are odd. Join them to make 2 rows of 8. That is 16. 16 is even.
